points.description: The answer conveys that a static array is initialized only once, when the function is first called, and not again on later calls.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (1.5) if the student says a static array is initialized once but does not tie this to the function call or to the first call.

points.description: The answer conveys that a non-static array is initialized every time the function is called, so the contrast with the static array is clear.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (1) if the student says a non-static array is re-initialized or reset without saying this happens on each function call.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the static behaviour (initialized once, at the first call) and the non-static contrast (initialized on every call). The central idea is the static array's one-time initialization, so it carries the larger share. A student who only describes one side, or who says only that static arrays are "initialized once" with no reference to function calls, earns partial credit. Equivalent wording is accepted.
